gap: No result ChatGPT got states a runtime measured at a microwave-sized load: The Solar Lab ran the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at a steady 1,479 W and it lasted 37.5 minutes, and OutdoorGearLab's usable-energy figures, taken at about 80% of each unit's rated output, work out to about 35–36 minutes at 1,500 W for the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (890 Wh each) and about 35 minutes for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 (870 Wh).
standout_why: I opened keeplights.com (microwave guide, cited), powerstationtips.com (cited), outletpowered.com (cited) and backuppowerfinder.com (cited). KeepLights, PowerStationTips and Outlet Powered give only calculated runtimes from an assumed 85% (or 0.95×0.85) usable share, and Outlet Powered says it 'did not physically test these products'. Backup Power Finder already lists OutdoorGearLab's 890/870/910/890 Wh usable-energy figures, which is why the score is not 3. It does not state OutdoorGearLab's test load, does not turn the figures into microwave minutes, and has no high-load runtime test. No page I opened has a timed run at about 1,500 W. unpluggedwatts.com and packcurrent.com would not open (certificate error), so I could not compare against them.
decides: Confirms the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 pick. OutdoorGearLab measured the same 890 Wh from it and from the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, and 870 Wh from the EcoFlow DELTA 3. Runtime per charge is therefore effectively a tie at about 35–36 minutes or about 17 two-minute reheats at 1,500 W, so the deciding factor is inverter headroom: the Anker's rated 2,000 W against 1,800 W. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 has the most measured energy (910 Wh), but The Solar Lab's 1,479 W run sat just under its 1,500 W ceiling. A 1,000 W-cooking microwave that draws about 1,500 W would leave it no margin. That supports the current page's verdict that it suits only a 700–900 W microwave.

findings.label: Measured runtime at a constant near-full load (microwave-class)
findings.source_title: Jackery 1000 V2 Review: Has Jackery Learned from Their Mistake? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'we ran a load of 1,479 watts—just shy of its maximum 1,500W capacity'. It lasted 37.5 minutes against an expected 43, which they report as 87.5% efficiency. 1,479 W × 37.5/60 ≈ 924 Wh delivered. The page gives no test date (2026 copyright only) and no named tester.

findings.label: Measured overload and surge behaviour
findings.value: held 1,560 W for about 10 min; shut off after a 2,200 W surge lasting a couple of seconds
findings.source_title: Jackery 1000 V2 Review: Has Jackery Learned from Their Mistake? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab stopped the 1,560 W run 'out of boredom'. Shows there is only about 60 W of tolerance above the 1,500 W rating.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 review (OutdoorGearLab), Kenji Mowrey, updated 2026-07-23
findings.note: Light-bar load bank at about 80% of rated max (about 1,200 W), per OutdoorGearLab's how-we-test page. 910 Wh ÷ 1,500 W = 36.4 min, but 1,500 W is this unit's continuous ceiling.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 review (OutdoorGearLab), Kenji Mowrey, updated 2026-07-23
findings.note: 'Using our light bar load bank, we measured 890 Wh out of its advertised 1,024 Wh.' The test load is about 80% of rated max (about 1,600 W), per the how-we-test page. At a 1,500 W microwave: 890/1,500×60 = 35.6 min, about 17 two-minute reheats. OutdoorGearLab's spec table wrongly shows 1,056 Wh, 1,800 W and 80%; the body text uses 1,024 Wh and 2,000 W. It also measured 25.2 lb and found the fan 'frustratingly loud' near max wattage.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy at a light load (EU 230 V unit)
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster: Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck), Marcus Schwarten, 2025-12-21, updated 2026-10-05
findings.note: EU version at 230 V, run down to the 1% cutoff. Notebookcheck also measured 1,110 Wh drawn during an AC recharge in just under 55 min, and about 45 dB at 1 m at high output. No microwave or 1,500 W+ test.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 review (OutdoorGearLab), Kenji Mowrey, updated 2026-07-23
findings.note: Load-bank test at about 80% of the 1,800 W rating (about 1,440 W). At 1,500 W: 870/1,500×60 = 34.8 min, about 17 two-minute reheats. No microwave test on the page.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy and kitchen-load note
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 100 V2 review (OutdoorGearLab), Kenji Mowrey, updated 2026-07-23
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab ran it at 80% of rated output with a quiet fan and said a toaster oven was 'handled easily'. Measured weight 25.0 lb. At 1,500 W: 35.6 min, the same as the C1000 Gen 2.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy (full discharge)
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 review (Digital Trends), Simon Sage, 2023-08-03
findings.note: Measured with an Emporia smart plug from 100% to empty; the load was not stated. Sage says it was the first station he had tested that could run his 'decrepit high-wattage microwave', but gives no draw or time figures. At 1,500 W: 976/1,500×60 ≈ 39 min.

findings.label: OutdoorGearLab capacity-test method
findings.value: load of about 80% of the unit's rated maximum wattage, applied with a light-bar jig; usable % = measured AC output ÷ claimed capacity
findings.note: This is why OutdoorGearLab's figures carry over to a microwave: the test load (about 1,200–1,600 W across these units) matches a 1,000 W-cooking microwave's 1,400–1,600 W input, unlike Notebookcheck's 250 W test. The page shows no date.

unsourced: PowerOffGrid's DELTA 3 microwave test (800 W microwave, 5 min, 100%→88% per the search snippet) and its AC180 microwave test (95%→93% in 2 min): poweroffgrid.com failed with a self-signed certificate error, so I could not open either page and left both out.
GoRV's Elite 100 V2 test with a 1,400 W microwave: gorv.com.au failed with the same certificate error, and the unit is likely the Australian 230 V model.

A timed microwave or about 1,500 W runtime test for the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and EcoFlow DELTA 3: not found at OutdoorGearLab, Notebookcheck, CleanTechnica (Kyle Field, 2025-09-24, no measured figures) or in two targeted searches.
OutdoorGearLab's exact per-unit test wattage: only the method page's 'approximately 80%' is published.
The test date of The Solar Lab's 1,479 W run: the page shows only a 2026 copyright.
A measured high-load figure for the BLUETTI AC180: Digital Trends' 976 Wh does not state the load.
